1.1: Welcome to JobDiva ATS Mastery. In this lesson, we introduce the Applicant Tracking System, or ATS — software that simplifies sourcing candidates and managing job orders. JobDiva is the ATS used company-wide at HonorVet Technologies, though other platforms like CEIPAL and Bullhorn exist across the staffing industry, and some companies even build their own in-house systems. What matters most as you get started is understanding that JobDiva uses role-based access: a SuperAdmin or Admin controls the entire system — creating users, configuring settings, and making organization-wide changes — while recruiters see only the portion relevant to their own work. This isn't a limitation to work around; it's intentional. Every user, from a brand-new recruiter to a senior account manager, receives individual login credentials, and those credentials are always provisioned by the SuperAdmin or coordinated through your manager — you'll never set up your own account from scratch. So if your screen looks different from a colleague's, or you don't see an icon someone else has, that's expected: your JobDiva view is calibrated specifically to your role and responsibilities within the organization, and it will grow as your role does.
1.2: Let's tour the upper bar of the JobDiva interface, starting with the universal search bar. You can search by candidate name, email, phone number, or Job ID and Reference ID, and JobDiva will also surface close matches — so even a partial or slightly-off search term can still return useful results. For the fastest, most precise search, though, use an exact Job ID, Reference ID, or email rather than a generic name, since names can be shared across many candidates. Next to search sits Favorites — a set of admin-preset shortcuts tailored to your specific role. You'll notice you can technically toggle these on and off yourself, but we strongly recommend leaving them alone, since they're already calibrated to what you actually need day to day. The Alerts icon shows your own JobDiva activity: status changes, new assignments, and job description edits, all in one place. Many of these alerts are triggered behind the scenes by VMS synchronization — sometimes called the Codler — an integration that automatically feeds job requirements from a client's Vendor Management System directly into JobDiva, so new positions and updates can appear without anyone manually re-entering them.
1.3: The News icon keeps you current on JobDiva enhancements and updates, including AI-assisted features like automated job description editing — and keep in mind that exactly which features are active depends on how your company has customized the platform. Under News, you'll also find a dedicated Training tab with role-specific webinars: there's one for recruiters, one for admins, one for client-relationship and business-development teams, one on advanced BI and reporting, one covering AI features, and — importantly — a dedicated healthcare recruiting track. If you're working in healthcare staffing, that webinar is genuinely worth your time, since it covers updates and workflows you won't find in the general training. For quick, in-the-moment answers, use the Help icon and the built-in chatbot before escalating a question to JobDiva support — most day-to-day questions about a specific feature can be resolved right there without ever opening a support ticket, and it's simply faster for everyone involved.
1.4: Your profile icon lets you sign out, verify your details, and confirm your division is set correctly — and if it's wrong, request a correction from your admin team rather than trying to work around it yourself, since the wrong division can affect what you're able to see and do elsewhere in the system. One essential, easy-to-overlook detail: accessing JobDiva outside office hours or off the office network requires a VPN, which is set up through your IT team, not something you can configure on your own. Finally, let's look at the left navigation. The Homepage icon always returns you to your role-based homepage, no matter how deep you've navigated into the system. The interface itself is organized into what are called Bars — grouped sections like Sourcing and Jobs — and each Bar contains individual Applications, which are the specific clickable tools you'll actually use every day. Understanding this Bars-and-Applications structure now will make everything in the rest of this course click into place much faster.
2.1: Your User Dashboard is a personal, fully customizable home base — and it's yours to shape around how you actually work. You can add or remove widgets like sales activity, current employees, submittal due dates, a weekly to-do list, and something called your active opportunity funnel, which gives you a visual sense of where your open deals stand. Here's the most important thing to understand about it: your dashboard is only as accurate as your data entry. If jobs and candidate actions aren't logged in real time — submissions, interviews, status changes — your dashboard simply won't reflect reality, no matter how well you've customized it. That's a discipline issue on the recruiter's side, not a limitation of JobDiva itself. The History section complements your dashboard by giving you a click-history log of every candidate, job, and page you've opened, filterable by date, so if you ever need to retrace your steps from earlier in the day or week, you can always find your way back without having to remember exact names or job numbers.
2.2: Before we go further, one important rule: never edit Settings yourself. Any change you need goes through your manager, who escalates it to the admin team or the SuperAdmin — this keeps the system consistent for everyone. Now let's look at the big picture. JobDiva is organized around four functional bars. Sourcing handles candidate management and allocation — this is where you'll spend a huge amount of your time. Jobs handles job management and allocation, working hand-in-hand with Sourcing. Analytics covers reporting and ratings, but access here is individually restricted by role, so don't be surprised if you can't see everything a manager can. And Engagement covers your calendar, tasks, and interviews — it's used somewhat differently between IT and healthcare recruiting, which we'll get into later in the course. As a recruiter, you'll spend most of your time living in Sourcing and Jobs, with Analytics and parts of Engagement being more manager-facing tools that you'll use occasionally rather than constantly.
3.1: Let's open the Jobs bar. My Jobs shows every open job currently assigned to you. My Jobs as Primary narrows that same list down to jobs where you're specifically the Primary Recruiter — meaning you carry lead responsibility for filling them, as opposed to a Secondary Recruiter, who's assigned to assist but doesn't own the outcome. There's a third role worth knowing here too: Primary Sales, which refers to the account manager you actually submit candidates to once you've found a match. When you need to search for a job rather than browse your assigned list, the fastest method by far is searching directly by its JobDiva ID or Reference ID. Remember the distinction: the JobDiva ID is generated automatically by the system the moment a job is created, while the Reference ID is the number assigned by the client itself. Searching by either of these IDs is dramatically faster and more reliable than typing in a job title, which can match dozens of similar postings across different clients.
3.2: Now let's create a job from scratch. You'll do this manually whenever automatic sync from a client's Vendor Management System fails, or when a requirement arrives by email instead of through the system. Accurately completing every structured field on this form — title, specialty, position type, division, client, facility, complete address, schedule, and billing details — is what we call JobDiva Cleaning, and it matters because every downstream step depends on this data being correct. Two details deserve special attention here. First, always select the Division that matches your own vertical, IT or healthcare, since the available options genuinely differ between the two, and picking the wrong one can misroute the job entirely. Second, never skip the Submitted Due Date field — it's mandatory, not optional, and job records without it create real confusion downstream for anyone tracking deadlines. And even though JobDiva doesn't currently use the bill rate to auto-calculate total compensation, enter it anyway; that data still matters for reporting and for anyone reviewing the job later.
3.3: With the core fields complete, it's time for Job Description Cleaning — and note this is a genuinely separate process from JobDiva Cleaning, focused purely on formatting the description text itself, since that text syncs live to external job boards and your company website the moment you save. A strong job description follows three parts: an introduction to the role, the required qualifications or must-haves, and any preferred or desired skills that are nice-to-have but not deal-breakers. Keep the formatting simple: minimal paragraph spacing, sparing use of highlights, and underline reserved only for section titles — a clean, scannable description reads far better to candidates than a dense wall of text. And here's a firm rule worth repeating: never include a client's sensitive or contract information in a public posting. If you want to share the client's actual name with a candidate, do that manually by email — don't put it in the posted description where anyone can see it.
3.4: Two tabs remain before saving. The Requirements tab captures a client's compliance needs — things like vaccination status, shift preferences, and other qualifications specific to that particular position — and this becomes especially important in healthcare, where it ties directly into what's called the Submittal Packet. The User tab is where a manager, and only a manager, assigns Primary and Secondary Recruiters along with Primary and Secondary Sales roles for the job. You as a recruiter can't self-assign here. The good news is you'll always know the moment you've been assigned, because JobDiva sends you an automatic email notification the instant it happens — no need to keep checking back. Once the Requirements and User tabs are in order, add any extra client context in the Remarks field, and click Save. That single action finalizes the job record and generates its unique JobDiva ID, which you'll use from that point forward to reference this exact position.
3.5: My Job Dashboard gives you a working view of every job assigned to you — issue date, division, title, location, client, bill and salary rate, status, priority, and submission activity, all laid out in one table so you can scan your entire workload at a glance. Two filters here are especially useful day to day. 'Open jobs with no submitters' flags positions assigned to you where you haven't submitted a single candidate yet — a clear signal about where to focus next. And 'pending interviews' flags jobs where an interview actually happened but its status was never updated in JobDiva, which is a paperwork gap, not a real scheduling problem. At the individual job level, there's also a cumulative dashboard that totals one position's submissions, interviews, and hires over its entire lifetime. Both views share the same dependency: their accuracy relies entirely on recruiters updating statuses in real time, in what's called the node section — something we'll cover in detail later in this course.
4.1: Analytics houses JobDiva's reporting tools, and it's worth knowing upfront that most of what lives here is manager-facing rather than something you'll use constantly as a recruiter. The Submittal Matrix Report checks submittals by user, department, or date range, and it's primarily a manager's tool for tracking recruiter output — submissions, interviews, and hires — across a team or time period. A related activity and summary report breaks the same kind of data down by client, group, or division instead of by individual user, which is useful for spotting patterns across an entire book of business. One thing to keep in mind: recruiter access to these reports is individually authorized, meaning your manager or admin controls exactly which reports you personally can open. So if a colleague can pull a report you can't see, that's not a bug — it simply reflects how access has been configured for your specific role, and if you genuinely need it for your work, that's a conversation to have with your manager.
4.2: The Engagement bar starts with My Calendar, where you can schedule events directly tied to your recruiting work — set a subject, link a specific candidate, choose a time and recurrence type, add a location and description, and save; JobDiva automatically emails the invite to everyone involved the moment you do. One thing worth flagging: Outlook sync for the calendar was noted as temporarily non-functional at the time this training was recorded, due to a known technical issue, so it's worth verifying the current status locally before relying on it for anything time-sensitive. Tasks work in a similar spirit to calendar events but for action items rather than meetings: you can assign a task to a colleague, a recruiter, a manager, or even a candidate, with a due date, a task type, and a completion percentage to track progress. Saving a task sends an immediate notification email to whoever it's assigned to, exactly like calendar events do — which is exactly why it's worth double-checking every detail before you hit save, since there's no quiet way to walk it back.
4.3: JobDiva includes two distinct interview tools, and it's worth understanding when each one fits. Live Interviews let you video-interview a candidate directly inside the platform — you can share an instant link for right now, or schedule a specific future time — as a genuine alternative to jumping into Teams or Zoom. E-Interviews work differently: they're a pre-built set of questions a candidate fills out asynchronously, on their own schedule, using text, multiple choice, audio, or even video answers, either before a live interview or sometimes instead of one entirely. Here's an important detail behind the video-answer option specifically: requiring a video response helps authenticate that the real candidate is the one actually answering, which matters because this is used deliberately in IT recruiting to catch proxy or forgery candidates — cases where someone other than the actual applicant tries to interview in their place. To send an e-interview, you build the questionnaire first, naming it, setting an expiration date, and defining each question's time limit and answer format, then look up the candidate and click Assign — which, like the other Engagement tools, immediately emails them the invitation.
5.1: We now arrive at Talent Search — genuinely the single most-used tool in a recruiter's day, accounting for an estimated eighty percent of daily work. It's worth slowing down here, because everything else in your sourcing workflow builds on what you learn in this module. Talent Search offers two fundamentally different approaches. Title Search looks for an exact job title match, like R-N or L-P-N, and returns a narrow, highly specific pool of candidates whose titles literally say that. Boolean Search, by contrast, is built from logical operators and returns a much broader set of results, including variations, synonyms, and related terms you might not have thought to type yourself. Neither approach is universally better — they're tools for different moments. Choose Title Search when you want a small, precise pool and you already know exactly what you're looking for. Choose Boolean Search when you want to expand your reach, combine multiple criteria, or you're not entirely sure which exact title a strong candidate might be using on their own resume.
5.2: Boolean search is built from six operators, and mastering them is genuinely foundational to everything else you'll do in Talent Search. AND requires both keywords to be present at the same time — RN AND ICU means a candidate needs both. OR returns results containing either keyword, which is especially useful for capturing title variations, like ICU OR Emergency Room. AND NOT includes the first keyword while explicitly excluding the second, letting you narrow a pool that's technically correct but too broad. Quotation marks force an exact multi-word phrase match — "registered nurse" as a phrase — and a rule worth remembering: quotation marks are never used around a single word, only genuine multi-word phrases. Parenthesis groups keywords together to control the logic and order of your search, and without it, a multi-part Boolean string becomes genuinely meaningless to the system — it simply can't parse what you intended. And finally, the asterisk, or wildcard, matches keyword variations, so manage-asterisk would catch managed, management, and managing — but here's the catch worth remembering: it is NOT supported inside JobDiva itself. It only works on external boards like Monster, Dice, or CareerBuilder. Building a genuinely strong Boolean string is a skill that improves with practice and real domain knowledge — there's no single fixed formula that works for every search.
5.3: On the Talent Search screen itself, Title Search offers a mapping toggle for exact-title refinement, plus a years-of-experience field to further narrow your pool by seniority. Boolean Search auto-builds your string as you add filters, and adding a Specialty from the preloaded list narrows an otherwise broad pool down to something much more usable — instead of manually typing every specialty term yourself. You can also choose how to source: real-time access across your assigned job boards, or a specific board with its own sort and filter options like relevancy, resume-updated date, or last-active date. From there, you can layer on location, licenses, certifications, and qualifications — but remember this guiding principle throughout: the lighter the string, the more the results. Specialty and title alone usually deliver strong outcomes on their own; stacking on every available filter tends to shrink your candidate pool far more than it helps narrow it meaningfully. There's also an Exclude field, which technically maps to AND NOT logic, but in practice it's often unnecessary once your search criteria is already clearly defined.
5.4: Now it's your turn. Using everything you've learned so far — AND, OR, AND NOT, quotation marks, and parenthesis — construct a Boolean string for this exact requirement: a registered nurse for a burn intensive care unit, with hospital experience required, needing both A-C-L-S and B-L-S certification. Take a genuine moment to write your string out before moving on. Think through it piece by piece: which terms need OR to capture title variations, which need AND to require multiple things at once, and — critically — where parenthesis needs to go to group those clauses correctly so the whole string actually parses the way you intend. Once you've written your version, compare it against the model answer described in the lesson notes, and pay particular attention to whether your parenthesis placement matches the intended logic. This is the exact live exercise given to trainees in the original session — treat it as a genuine checkpoint before moving forward, not something to skip past.
6.1: There are four distinct ways to add a new candidate to JobDiva, and it's worth knowing all four since different situations call for different ones. Upload lets you select a resume file directly — just keep it under five megabytes — and once it's processed, verify the auto-extracted Personal Info, Professional Specialty, and Work Experience sections before submitting, since automated parsing isn't always perfect. Dedicated email upload works differently: you simply email the resume to a dedicated address, and you'll get a confirmation once it's been added to the system — no manual data entry required on your end. Copy-paste lets you select a source, or none at all, and paste the full resume text directly into the field. And manual entry lets you add just a few key details and save, creating a bare candidate record when you don't have a full resume in hand. One field deserves special attention here: the Professional Specialty section is explicitly called out as very important specifically for healthcare resumes, so don't skip it even when you're moving quickly. And regardless of which method you use, always verify the auto-extracted fields before clicking Submit — never trust automated parsing blindly.
6.2: To find an existing candidate rather than add a new one, Lookup a Candidate works fastest when you have a name, email, and phone number together — the more of these three you can provide, the more precisely JobDiva narrows the match. Search Candidate takes a slightly different approach, letting you filter by contact info or by professional specialty and profession, which is useful when you're browsing rather than looking for one specific person. There's also an important distinction worth understanding clearly: an employee is someone who's already been placed, while a candidate is still somewhere in sourcing or submittal, not yet working. That status only changes from candidate to employee after a very specific sequence: an interview happens, the candidate accepts, the client confirms onboarding, and finally a Start is formally recorded inside JobDiva. Nobody manually types 'employee' anywhere — it's a system consequence of that Start being properly recorded, which we'll cover in much more depth later in this course when we walk through the full HireTrack process.
6.3: A Hot List is your personal, curated list of favorite candidates for a specific role — and it does more than just save your picks, since it also automatically fetches new matching resumes based on a saved search string you define once and let run in the background. To build one, click New Hot List, define your search criteria using Boolean logic plus specialty and state, name that saved string clearly, and link it to the relevant job before saving. One important boundary here: never assign users, groups, or divisions to a hot list yourself — that's reserved specifically for managers. Once your hot list exists, adding a favorite candidate is as simple as clicking its dedicated icon, then refreshing to confirm it stuck; removing works the same way, either from the hot list itself or from the candidate's own profile page. Two viewing options round this out: Preview shows a short candidate summary right inline without leaving the page, while Expand shows considerably more detail, including how a candidate's actual years of experience stack up against what your saved criteria requires.
6.4: Search Candidate Notes filters by note content, action, and date — but only works well with standardized note actions, like RTR Log or RTR Signed and Interviewed, rather than informal shorthand like 'logged' or 'DNC.' Attributes capture submittal-required details, like the last four SSN digits and date of birth, tied to the quality-audit process — they must be filled in for every submission, or it won't pass audit.
7.1: When you have many resumes to add at once rather than one at a time, use Bulk Upload instead of the standard New Candidate flow. Select your source first, optionally link the entire batch to a hot list right from the same screen — which saves you a separate step later — and then upload, keeping in mind the hard limit of fewer than fifty files per single batch. This is genuinely one of the biggest time-savers available when you're processing a large stack of resumes from a career fair, a referral drive, or a bulk email from a vendor, since doing them one by one through New Candidate would take far longer for exactly the same result.
7.2: The Job toolbar includes two handy shortcuts worth knowing: Clone, which duplicates an existing job under a brand-new JobDiva ID — useful when a client reopens a nearly identical position — and Merge, which combines two job records and lets you choose which details from each to keep. When it comes to posting a job to LinkedIn, remember this firm sequence, because it trips people up constantly: the job must be Open, Assigned, and Saved before the LinkedIn posting fields even appear on screen. LinkedIn posting always uses your company's integrated account, never a personal one — you'll set the contract ID, degree, industry, employment status, and expiry date, then post. Expect a short backend delay before it actually goes live, so don't assume something failed if it's not instant. And keep in mind that company-portal and Monster or Dice posting from directly within JobDiva depends on whether integration slots are available for your account; otherwise, you'll post directly on those platforms instead.
7.3: Job Applicants shows everyone who applied through an integrated portal or directly through your company website, all funneled into one place; accepting an applicant automatically creates their candidate profile for you, no manual entry required. Email Job lets you send the position directly to a candidate by email — but always confirm the right template with your manager first rather than defaulting to whatever's preloaded, since templates are often client- or role-specific and using the wrong one can send mixed signals. And Email Merge tracking shows you, per job, exactly who received your outreach, whether they actually opened it, and what action followed afterward, giving you a real feedback loop on how effective your outreach has been rather than just sending emails into the void.
7.4: Harvest is JobDiva's automated sourcing engine — once you activate it on a saved search string, it continuously feeds matching resumes from the internal database straight into an active job, working in the background even while you're focused on something else. Toggle it on or off using Schedule and Not Schedule, and always remember to click Save afterward; the toggle genuinely has no effect until you do; a lot of recruiters assume it's active the moment they flip the switch, and it simply isn't. There's also an AI feature that can suggest a search-criteria string based on the job description itself, which is a great starting point if you're not sure where to begin building your own string. Beyond Harvest, you can also post a job to VPN — a staffing job-posting network — directly from the User field: select VPN, click Post on VPN, add travel or weekly rate details along with any shift information, and save. Expect roughly thirty to forty-five minutes before it actually reflects live, so don't panic if it's not there instantly.
8.1: The Activities section logs every submission, interview update, and Start performed by any team member on a given job — which makes it genuinely worth checking before you submit a candidate yourself, simply to avoid duplicating a colleague's work on the exact same position. That said, the trainer specifically recommends performing your actual submissions from the candidate's own profile rather than directly from Activities, since that path carries more of the relevant candidate context along with it automatically. From there, the Search Criteria page shows resumes matching your applied search in real time, updating as new matches come in, with a Preview option for a quick inline summary and an Expand option when you need considerably more detail on a specific candidate before deciding whether to move forward with them.
8.2: Email Merge lets you reach many candidates at once with a single templated message — a genuinely powerful way to accelerate sourcing when you have a large qualified pool and limited time to call everyone individually. The workflow runs like this: confirm your relevant candidate list, select a sender email and template, choose your batch size, optionally skip candidates you've already contacted for similar roles, then 'beautify' the template — adding job description highlights, urgent-hiring framing, location details, and either an IT- or healthcare-specific template already saved to the job, or one your manager provides — add your signature, and send. Here's the critical guidance to actually remember: keep each batch at or under roughly three hundred recipients. Going bigger risks your email getting flagged as spam, and it can genuinely draw scrutiny from your own IT team over unusual outbound volume from your account. And always check for, and honor, any candidate's specific request to be excluded from future mass outreach — that's not optional courtesy, it's a compliance expectation.
8.3: A candidate's Availability status — available, unavailable, or unavailable indefinitely, along with a note explaining why — is visible to every recruiter who shares access to that candidate, which is genuinely valuable because it prevents multiple people from redundantly calling someone who's already said no. The opt-out link lets a candidate stop receiving emails entirely, with a matching opt-in option if they later change their mind. Do Not Submit flags a specific client that a candidate should never be submitted to, along with a documented reason — and note that this feature has to be admin-enabled per user before you can use it yourself. One firm rule here, learned directly from a real mistake the trainer observed on the team: never, under any circumstances, delete a candidate's resume from the Candidate Information section. It's treated as a serious, entirely avoidable error, and there's simply no good reason to ever do it.
8.4: Licenses, certifications, and qualifications aren't just administrative record-keeping — they directly power your search results down the line. Add license and certification details complete with expiration dates, and enable automatic expiration alerts where appropriate so candidates get reminded before something lapses without anyone having to track it manually. Just as important: always tag a candidate's Profession and Specialty, and fill in their Qualifications, things like work authorization and shift preference. Skip these fields, and a filtered search — say, for a specific work-authorization status — will return few or no results, even when perfectly qualified candidates genuinely exist somewhere in your database. This isn't a one-time task; it's long-term team hygiene that compounds into dramatically stronger search results over months and years, which is exactly why the trainer keeps returning to this point throughout the course.
9.1: Now we reach the heart of the HireTrack process: ownership and Right to Represent, or R-T-R. Before you can claim ownership of a candidate submission, you must first obtain their authorization — either by text message or a signed RTR document — and this order matters enormously. Claiming ownership without RTR first is a real mistake to actively avoid; it was specifically called out as creating ownership artificially, without the candidate's actual consent ever being given. The Node section is where you log every action and every conversation status each time you work a candidate, so your teammates always know the current state of that relationship before they reach out themselves and risk stepping on each other's outreach. Ownership taken through this process typically holds for one week, and there's a healthcare-specific phone screening template available specifically for recording detailed discussion notes during that initial conversation with a candidate.
9.2: Here's the internal submission workflow, laid out step by step: select the assigned job by its ID, confirm the position type, attach the candidate's latest resume, choose the manager or Primary Sales contact you're submitting to, enter the aggregate bill and pay rate, confirm the submission date, time, and time zone, and add your internal notes. Once you save, JobDiva automatically emails the submission — including a concise clinical profile, a background summary, a rating, and any honest concerns — directly to the decision-maker on the other end. This single workflow effectively replaces what used to be a manual, back-and-forth request to a manager, and it's especially valuable if you're working remotely, since you're not dependent on catching someone at their desk. One regional note worth knowing: 'cop to cop' rate arrangements are generally not used in healthcare staffing specifically, so don't expect to see that structure come up often in this vertical.
9.3: From an internal submission, a manager can either reject the candidate outright or move forward to external submission with the actual client. When it comes to updating interview details afterward, the single most important thing to get exactly right is the date, time, and time zone together — confirm all three directly with the hiring manager rather than assuming, since a time-zone mismatch here can cause a candidate to miss an interview entirely through no fault of their own. Recording a Start — the action that officially marks a candidate as placed — is normally restricted to managers and DMs rather than individual recruiters, though it's still essential that you understand exactly how the process works end to end, since you'll often be the one gathering the details that go into it even if you're not the one clicking the final button.
9.4: A few remaining tools round out the candidate profile. The Wallet aggregates a candidate's certifications, licenses, attachments, and RTR record in one place — keeping it complete saves the whole team repeat verification calls. Resume tools let you upload, download, print, and email a resume, and Find Ideal Job surfaces matching open jobs automatically. Diva Match shows a percentage match between a candidate and open jobs — but always verify a matched job's real status on the client's own portal, since JobDiva's status can occasionally lag behind reality.
9.5: Let's recap the full journey we've covered in this course. Start with sourcing through Talent Search using Boolean logic, bring candidates in through New Candidate intake, organize and reach out through Hot Lists and Email Merge, secure Right to Represent before ever claiming ownership, move through internal and then external submission, track the interview carefully, and finally record the Start that completes the placement and converts a candidate into an employee. Supporting all of this throughout are the Wallet, resume tools, Diva Match, Notes and Attributes, and Outlook-integrated email tracking — the connective tissue that keeps every step accountable and searchable. And running underneath the entire course are the healthcare-specific threads worth remembering: Professional Specialty tagging, Submittal Packets, phone screening templates, licenses and compact licenses, and BLS and ACLS certifications. Every single tool in this course exists to support one linear journey — source, engage, submit, and place. Congratulations on completing JobDiva ATS Mastery.
